newsitem.title: GERMANY: E. German state sees higher grain, rapeseed crops.
newsitem.headline: E. German state sees higher grain, rapeseed crops.

text.p: The eastern German state of Mecklenburg expects higher grain and rapeseed crops in 1997, based on good weather and area expansions, its statistics office said in a report.
Mecklenburg is Germany's leading oilseeds producer and the report was based on a farmers' survey.
Mecklenburg's winter and spring rapeseed crop may range between 500,000 and 600,000 tonnes versus only 330,000 tonnes in 1996 when the severe 1995/96 winter had killed parts of the crop.
The office said winter rapeseed yields may be 3.1 tonnes per hectare (tph) compared with 1.96 tph last year.
The winter rapeseed acreage was expanded by 17 percent to 170,000 ha while spring rape areas dropped 46 percent to 15,000 ha.

A source at the statistics office said weather patterns during autumn plantings of grain and rapeseed had been ideal and the harsh 1996/97 winter had been unable to hurt rapeseed, wheat, rye and barley.
But spring barley and oats had suffered from spring frosts.
The state was expecting an overall grain crop of 3.5 million tonnes, up 500,000 from 1996.
Yield forecasts were detailed as follows -- winter wheat 6.7 tph (6.3 tph in 1996), rye 5.4 tph (5.2), winter barley 6.2 tph (4.6), triticale 6.0 tph (5.6).
Spring barley and oats yields of 4.9 tph each compared with 5.1 and 5.2 tph respectively in 1996.
